title: Berlin Hiking Trails - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has twenty numbered, signposted long-distance footpaths**, the Grüne Hauptwege, and the marked network covers **about 575 km**. Eighteen run from one edge of the city to another. Two are rings: the Innerer Parkring (52 km) and the Tiergartenring (23 km).

**You do not walk a route, you walk a stage of it.** Counting a station as on a route when it sits within 1 km of the line, **282 station points touch the twenty routes across 195 different stations**, which gives **3,684 station-to-station walks**. About 1,883 of those are between 2 and 12 km.

**Rail access is wildly uneven.** The Tiergartenring has 28 stations on 23 km and never more than 2.5 km between two of them. The Spandauer Weg has two stations on 33 km, and the first 16.7 km has none. Weg 1 holds the longest empty stretch on the network, 17.6 km from S Spindlersfeld to Erkner.

**Only eight of the twenty routes have a rail station at both official ends**, and four of them (2, 4, 16 and 20) have one at neither, which is why the official start is sometimes a bus stop or a ferry pier.

**The Senate says these are hiking routes, not accessible paths**: steps, high kerbs, poor or missing lighting, and no claim to extra traffic safety. Some sections cross allotments, cemeteries and parks that lock their gates in the evening.

**Autumn takes the afternoon away twice.** Sunset is 19:28 on 13 September, 17:54 on 24 October and **16:52 on 25 October** once the clocks go back. Tempelhofer Feld, which starts and ends the Innerer Parkring, shuts at 21:30 in September and **19:00 from 1 October**.
**Route files are free.** GPX, KML and printable PDF for all twenty routes come from the Senate's own download page, and the waymark to follow is a white hiking bear on a green square.
